claims.summary: JSON_VALUE performs classic scalar-path extraction from JSON text in the documented SQL Server 2016+/Azure SQL scope. This expression omits the supplied result wrapper and therefore does not locate the answer. Its path would fit a variable containing only the unwrapped provider result, which is not the shown input.

The given tree places the short scalar answer at result.choices[0].message.content, exactly the path demonstrated by the training. The product reference establishes the classic supported scalar operation; the supplied under-200-character string fits its ordinary nvarchar(4000) result. This does not assert an arbitrary-length or universal provider-envelope contract.

The JSON_QUERY product reference establishes the classic SQL Server 2016+/Azure SQL object/array extraction operation and its default lax-mode behavior. The selected value here is a scalar string, so JSON_QUERY does not extract the answer as the requested scalar. It would suit an actual object or array at that path in a different supplied response.

Classic JSON_VALUE can extract the scalar at the HTTP-code path, but the shown value is metadata 200 rather than the answer string. That path is appropriate when the task is to read the supplied transport status. No assertion about invoking the REST procedure or its feature maturity is needed to interpret this literal JSON document.
